gold.question: Regarding P-1-1 on the P&ID: It won't prime anymore, it used to. What should I check first?

gold.question: Regarding GV-1-2 on the P&ID: It hums but won't open. What could be wrong?

candidate: GV-1-2 is a globe valve served by the GFPS Type 165 2/2-way solenoid valve datasheet, and a humming coil that fails to open points to a few causes described there. The valve is servo-controlled and requires a minimum differential pressure of 0.5 bar to open and close, so if the pressure differential across it is below 0.5 bar it will energize (hum) but not open. The datasheet also specifies the media must be clean liquids without solid particles, so debris or particles in the line could be blocking or jamming the diaphragm/insert so the pilot cannot actuate. Additionally, the supply voltage must be within the stated tolerance of ±10% (24V DC, 230V or 115V 50/60 Hz depending on the coil fitted); an out-of-tolerance or wrong-voltage supply can leave the coil humming without enough force to shift the valve. Checking the differential pressure, media cleanliness, and coil voltage against the datasheet's technical data would be the appropriate troubleshooting steps.

gold.question: Regarding GV-1-2 on the P&ID: It hums but won't open. What could be wrong?

candidate: GV-1-2 is a servo-controlled 2/2-way diaphragm solenoid valve (Type 165, fail-safe to close). The humming indicates the coil is energized, so the likely fault is hydraulic rather than electrical: this servo-operated valve needs a minimum differential pressure of 0.5 bar to open and close, and its working pressure range is 0.5–6 bar. If the differential pressure across the valve is below 0.5 bar (or the upstream pressure is too low), the pilot/diaphragm cannot lift and the valve stays closed while the coil hums. Other contributing possibilities consistent with the datasheet are a supply voltage outside the ±10% tolerance (weakening the coil), or media contamination — the valve is rated only for clean liquids without solid particles, so debris could be blocking the servo passage.
